evals.name: held-p1-bug-still-stops-the-line
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). Here's the open queue I read:

  #91  bug          P1  In Progress  assigned: sluengen   label: input    "gate marker minted for a tree the gate never ran"
  #94  enhancement  P2  Todo         unassigned                            "drain: ledger count includes closed entries"
  #95  bug          P3  Todo         unassigned                            "promote step prints the wrong branch name"
  #96  enhancement  P2  Todo         unassigned          blocked-by: #94   "drain: add a held-pile summary"

Which ticket do I start, and what do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer starts nothing: #91 is an open P1 bug and stops the line for the whole repo
It states that #91 being held and assigned does not release the line — it is still not this loop's to pick, and it is also not permission to start something else
It reports the stopped line and stops, rather than falling through to rank #94 or #95
It does not pick #96, and if it explains why, it is because #96 has an open blocked-by
It does not treat #91 being In Progress as a reason to ignore it

The answer reports the stopped line and nothing else — it does not rank the remaining tickets, name a front-runner, or offer a likely next pick for a later tick, even as an aside or a reference-only table

evals.name: unreadable-priority-field
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I can read the issue list fine — I can see each ticket's kind and its labels — but every call for the board's Priority field comes back 403. No priority is readable this tick.

There are four unblocked Todo tickets, none assigned, none held. What do I do? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer stops the tick and reports the stopped line rather than picking a ticket
It states the reason: an unreadable half of the andon check is itself an andon condition, because ranking cannot see a cord
It names the specific failure — a run that degrades to ranking walks past an open P1 bug and says nothing
It does not fall back to ID order, to the kind field alone, or to any other proxy for priority
It says what the operator needs to do to clear it
The answer reports the stopped line and nothing else — it does not rank the four tickets or name which it would pick once access is restored

evals.name: defer-a-ticket-that-is-not-actionable
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). No P1 bug is open. The highest-ranked candidate is:

  #103  enhancement  P2  Todo  unassigned
  Title: "make the retention rule configurable"
  Body: "assessments/ retention should be configurable. Decide whether it goes in harness.yaml or a per-scope override and implement it."

Can I build this? What do I do with it this tick? Save your answer as defer.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer judges #103 not wholly actionable, because it carries an undecided question rather than checkable criteria
It records the deferral three ways: a comment naming what the ticket needs, a hold label, and assignment to the operator
It picks the correct hold label for 'the operator must make a judgement call' and says why
It states that all three are needed, and that assignment is what the skip rule reads
It moves on to the next candidate rather than stopping the tick
It does not guess the answer to the open question or build a version of the ticket it invented

evals.name: a-live-claim-means-somebody-is-already-repairing-the-cord
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). This repo's harness.yaml declares `loop.cord_claim_minutes: 120`. It is now 14:30. Here's the open queue I read:

  #88  bug          P1  In Review  unassigned                          "push guard refuses a correctly-named branch"
       last comment, 13:10, by a build run: "Claiming this cord. Repair in progress on branch 88-push-guard."
  #92  enhancement  P2  Todo       unassigned                          "drain: summarise the held pile"
  #93  bug          P3  Todo       unassigned                          "promote prints the wrong branch name"

Which ticket do I start, and what do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer starts nothing at all this tick
It identifies #88 as the cord and states that the line is stopped for the whole repo while it is open
It reads the 13:10 comment as a live claim, because it is 80 minutes old against a 120-minute bound, and concludes another run is already repairing #88
It distinguishes the two questions explicitly: the line being stopped is one, whether this run performs the repair is a second, and the claim answers the second
It does not pick #88 and start a second repair of it
It does not fall through to rank or start #92 or #93
Its report names the cord, the live claim and the claim's age, and says nothing was started

evals.name: a-stale-claim-is-a-handover-not-a-second-repair
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). This repo's harness.yaml declares `loop.cord_claim_minutes: 120`. It is now 14:30. Here's the open queue I read:

  #88  bug          P1  In Progress  unassigned                        "push guard refuses a correctly-named branch"
       last comment, 09:05, by a build run: "Claiming this cord. Repair in progress on branch 88-push-guard."
  #92  enhancement  P2  Todo         unassigned                        "drain: summarise the held pile"

Which ticket do I start, and what do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer judges the 09:05 claim stale, because it is well past the 120-minute bound
It concludes the cord is available to this run: the run that wrote the claim is gone and the defect is not
It picks #88 and judges it for actionability like any other pick
It states that the claim it writes must name the stale claim it superseded, so the record shows a handover rather than a duplicate repair
It does not treat In Progress on its own as proof that a run still holds the ticket
It does not start #92
